known_bugs: The exact Windows 10 19045 Intel-GPU and WebView2 foreground behavior is not reproducible headlessly. v0.5.22 encodes the observed workaround and verifies window postconditions, but the user's target machine remains the final runtime acceptance.

The no-sandbox Codex argument is a security-reducing last-resort fallback. It is child-scoped and remembered only after a successful exact-version launch; users requiring full Chromium sandboxing must resolve the underlying driver/OS incompatibility.

Legacy portable tests had real HKCU/StartMenu mutation; now test-gated. Two synthetic developer-host metadata entries and one tiny failed media fixture remain because exact cleanup was denied by tool policy; no bypass attempted. Details in v0.5.8-uninstall-audit.md section6.

Uninstall erases only confirmed product-owned/current-user scope. Shared runtimes, OS logs, unknown legacy volume ownership/registry originals, other users and copied untracked kits are intentionally preserved; actual target machine lifecycle is not proven by mocks.
Real USB AppX deployment, machine HKLM permissions, UAC and runtime installation on a blank PC are not covered by host mock/static tests.

Protected ACLs, enterprise policies, unsupported Home/stripped Windows behavior, broken AppX services, pending servicing and disk faults may still block installation; security restrictions are not overridden.
Machine-wide AppX data policy uses a per-user recovery journal; one Windows account is the supported baseline, not concurrent multi-user reference counting or alternate-administrator credentials.
Keep-data AppX removal preserves a verified recoverable backup, not automatic reimport into a later installation.
Unsigned development license is not production anti-copy enforcement; program on USB is not a guarantee of fixed-time process termination when unplugged.
Unrelated existing engine formatting differences remain; scoped formatter checks and all recorded test/build/verification commands pass.
done_criteria: New USB installs use verified MSIX extraction into apps/Codex and keep mutable data in the normal local Windows profile
USB Codex and CCSwitch launch success requires a stable sizeable window, with child-scoped compatibility and exact-root cleanup
Program-level uninstall is idempotent and has retry/postcondition checks within the current-user ownership boundary
Superseded process-guard development document is removed/marked historical
Relevant tests, cross-target checks and release static verification pass
The Windows entrypoint has no dynamic VC runtime imports and the bundled VC redist is hash/signature verified
The USB entrypoint automatically requests a standard runas UAC confirmation and refuses to continue without a verified elevated token; normal local manager startup remains unaffected
Remaining work is explicitly limited to real Windows acceptance
historical_known_bugs: Current release now retries an Add-AppxVolume Access denied result with a narrowly scoped UAC registration; real clean-machine acceptance must confirm the Windows prompt and volume publication
Real AppXVolume/UAC/filesystem compatibility is not covered by the host simulation; latest release still needs a clean-machine rerun with operation diagnostics
Codex launched directly from Start menu may remain cached after unplug; USB mode does not promise a fixed kill deadline
Unsigned development bundles auto-enroll the USB license; anti-copy release requires a pre-provisioned signed license
CCSwitch data-directory behavior must be confirmed against the exact shipped build
All-user/provisioned AppX packages and enterprise-locked policy are reported, not forcibly deleted
External portable Codex/CCSwitch directories without this product's ownership proof are intentionally left untouched
Full npm test has a host WSL/bash fixture failure in release-workflow

Real AppXVolume/UAC/filesystem behavior still needs clean-machine acceptance; the USB URI path now tries WinRT PackageManager.AddPackageAsync, then explicit system-volume bootstrap plus Move-AppxPackage recovery, but Windows policy/storage hardware can still reject deployment
The clean-machine VC++ bootstrap has not been run on a machine missing the runtime; the Microsoft installer may still be blocked by UAC, Windows Installer busy (1618), or security software

On the user's removable D: volume, the 802 MB MSIX Authenticode PowerShell probe previously exceeded the 45-second RunLimits::probe deadline; production now defers the scan until a local staged copy and uses a dedicated 5-minute bounded deadline

Real blank-machine VC++ bootstrap, AppXVolume registration and package deployment are not reproducible in host tests; the final bundle passes static Authenticode/metadata checks but still needs a clean Windows 10/11 acceptance
Release scripts now handle Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM/default-path cases; scripts that depend on GitHub CLI or a real MSIX still require their external prerequisites
Automatic USB startup elevation still requires the user to approve UAC; a standard account, cancelled prompt, UAC-disabled-by-policy state or enterprise AppX policy cannot be legally forced through
MachinePolicy/UserPolicy, WDAC or AppLocker may still block PowerShell even with the process-local Bypass compatibility switch; this is an administrator-controlled boundary

The standalone launcher makes the initial UAC token deterministic, but a cancelled/denied UAC prompt, standard-account credential handoff, enterprise policy, unsupported removable AppX volume or security software can still block installation
v0.5.4 real Add-AppxPackage/WinRT placement on a target removable NTFS volume remains unverified by host tests; failure now stops/cleans rather than silently accepting C:

For non-deployment sideload packages, Windows may reject PreserveApplicationData with 0x80073CFA; v0.5.6 retries without the flag, and old AppX modules without the optional parameter also use the explicit no-preserve path, so package-local data cannot be guaranteed on either compatibility path

The v0.5.6 launcher/manager smoke with a live guard lease is intentionally not a finite test: --codex-usb-guard is a long-running monitor and must be tested with a missing/temporary lease or by the real manager lifecycle
